newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan coalition jets bomb Herat.
newsitem.headline: Afghan coalition jets bomb Herat.

text.p: Warplanes of coalition forces fighting the radical Islamic Taleban militia bombed the western Afghan city of Herat late on Tuesday but caused no damage, a Taleban spokesman said on Wednesday.

The Peshawar-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted a Taleban spokesman as saying three Russian-made SU-27 fighter jets bombed Taleban tank positions eight kilometres (five miles) west of Herat but caused no damage.
The AIP quoted witnesses as saying at least two people were wounded in the attack.
The spokesman said the attack on Herat, the main Taleban base in the west, followed advances by the Islamic militia in the remote northwestern province of Badghis over the past two weeks.

The Taleban, who took control of the Afghan capital Kabul in late September, are fighting in Badghis against the alliance of northern Uzbek chief Abdul Rashid Dostum and Ahmad Shah Masood, military chief of the ousted government.
Both sides have claimed victories in the area, but there have been no independent accounts of the fighting.
Just north of Kabul, however, the Taleban have pushed the coalition forces back over the past few days, witnesses said.
